title: Chartwise etale permanence for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Call a morphism $f:X\to Y$ chartwise etale if for every representable etale map $U\to X$ from a scheme $U$, the composite $U\to Y$ is representable etale; representable etale means that every base change to a scheme is an etale morphism of schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism whose source is a scheme, chartwise etale is equivalent to representable etale. Identity morphisms are chartwise etale. Composites of chartwise etale morphisms are chartwise etale, and their base changes by arbitrary morphisms of algebraic spaces are chartwise etale. If $X\to Z$ and $Y\to Z$ are chartwise etale, every morphism $X\to Y$ over $Z$ is chartwise etale. A family is an etale covering when all its maps are chartwise etale and it is jointly surjective on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Isomorphisms give singleton etale coverings; composites of etale coverings are etale coverings; and for every etale covering $\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ and every map $X'\to X$, the family $\{X'\times_XX_i\to X'\}_{i\in I}$ is an etale covering. The fibre products here are sheaf fibre products of algebraic spaces [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

proof.text: For a scheme-source $f$, test chartwise etaleness on its identity; the converse follows by representable composition, using [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Identity maps preserve each chart, and the chartwise quantifiers applied successively prove composition. Isomorphisms are representable etale by the same node, hence are chartwise etale by composition with each chart.

source.place: Tag 03FR and its following paragraph; Tag 03FT.

proof.text: For chartwise etale f:X→Z and g:Y→Z, set P=Y×_Z X and choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas a:U→X using [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection]. Form R=P×_X U using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The cover p:R→P is representable surjective etale: for any scheme test, lift the representing square for a into this pullback and use pullback cancellation. Pasting R→U over P→X with P→X over Y→Z identifies R→Y as the base change of a followed by f. This composite is representable etale by the chartwise hypothesis; the same scheme-test pullback argument therefore makes R→Y representable etale. Apply part (2) of [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection] to p and P→Y.

source.place: Tag 03FU: the atlas argument, with source-cover detection supplying the omitted verification.

proof.text: Let $hf=g$ with $g:X\to Z$ and $h:Y\to Z$ chartwise etale. Given a scheme chart $a:U\to X$, choose an atlas $b:V\to Y$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], $W=U\times_YV$ is a scheme, $p:W\to U$ is surjective etale, and $gap$ and $hb$ are representable etale. Its comparison clause applied to $(hb)r=gap$, for $r:W\to V$, makes $r$ etale. Therefore $br=fap$ is representable etale by that node. Part (1) of [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection] makes $fa$ representable etale. This holds for every chart $a$, proving cancellation.

The isomorphism and composition clauses of [lem-trf-presheaf-field-lift-family-calculus] give joint surjectivity for singleton isomorphisms and composite families. For base change, lift the image of a field-valued section of X′ through the original family after a field extension. Naturality identifies the image of the restricted section of X′ with the image of this lift. The forgetful functor from sheaves preserves the pullback, and evaluation gives a pullback of types, so the compatible pair supplies a field-valued section of the actual sheaf fibre product. Its first projection is the required restriction of the original section. The chartwise base-change result gives etaleness of every member. Empty families satisfy the same argument: a target field-valued section would contradict the lifting hypothesis. The fibre products are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), clauses (1)-(3); point-lifting clauses separated from chartwise etaleness.

lean.statement: theorem chartwise_etale_permanence {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (T : Over S) (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : schemeSpace T ⟶ Y), IsChartwiseEtale f ↔ IsEtale f.hom.hom) ∧ (∀ X : AlgebraicSpace S, IsChartwiseEtale (𝟙 X)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), IsChartwiseEtale f → IsChartwiseEtale g → IsChartwiseEtale (f ≫ g)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z), IsChartwiseEtale f → IsChartwiseEtale (enlargedFibreProductFst g f)) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : X ⟶ Z) (h : Y ⟶ Z) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsChartwiseEtale g → IsChartwiseEtale h → f ≫ h = g → IsChartwiseEtale f) ∧ (∀ (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (e : X ≅ Y), IsChartwiseEtale e.hom ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ e.hom.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (J : I → Type v) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢⱼ : ∀ i : I, J i → AlgebraicSpace S) (f : ∀ i : I, Xᵢ i ⟶ X) (g : ∀ (i : I) (j : J i), Xᵢⱼ i j ⟶ Xᵢ i), ((∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (f i)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (f i).hom.hom)) → (∀ i : I, (∀ j : J i, IsChartwiseEtale (g i j)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun j : J i ↦ (g i j).hom.hom)) → (∀ a : Sigma J, IsChartwiseEtale (g a.1 a.2 ≫ f a.1)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun a : Sigma J ↦ (g a.1 a.2 ≫ f a.1).hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (X X' : AlgebraicSpace S) (Xᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (f : ∀ i : I, Xᵢ i ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X), ((∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (f i)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (f i).hom.hom)) → (∀ i : I, IsChartwiseEtale (enlargedFibreProductFst g (f i))) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (enlargedFibreProductFst g (f i)).hom.hom))
